biography.plain_text: Anthony Wayne March is a former adviser who operated Asset Trader, a North Carolina nonprofit selling charitable gift annuities and exit-planning products. He pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud after using investor money for personal and scheme expenses. In 2021, he received a 135-month prison sentence and a restitution order exceeding $6 million.

long_biography.plain_text:
In 2013, March and a partner established The Life Asset Bond Company in Luxembourg, with March owning virtually all its shares. The company's articles allowed it to make loans, issue debt and hold investments or real estate. In North Carolina, March also led Asset Trader, a tax-exempt nonprofit that presented itself as an educator in exit planning.

Asset Trader solicited more than $8.1 million from at least 22 people for charitable gift annuities and related products. The organisation did not use their money for the stated charitable purpose. March admitted conspiracy to commit wire fraud. The court imposed imprisonment and restitution; federal records show that he remained incarcerated while pursuing post-conviction relief.
